description_summary: The full GTA 6 money guide from early game to mid game: store stick-ups, Kenton's treasure diving, Moses's car contracts, gang hideouts, high-end stores and banks, plus how to protect your cash and the truth about the money cheat.

beats.caption: Money in GTA 6 matters more than in any GTA before it. Guns, cars, clothes, all of it costs cash, and some story missions won't even start until you have enough of it in your pocket.
beats.tts: Money in GTA 6 matters more than in any GTA before it. Guns, cars, clothes, all of it costs cash, and some story missions won't even start until you have enough of it in your pocket.
beats.visual_need: Vice City skyline, cash being counted

beats.caption: So in this video I'll give you the full money route from the early game to the mid game. What to do first, what to skip, and the one mistake that can wipe out everything you've earned in a single second.
beats.tts: So in this video I'll give you the full money route from the early game to the mid game. What to do first, what to skip, and the one mistake that can wipe out everything you've earned in a single second.
beats.visual_need: fast montage of robbery, car chase, diving

beats.caption: Here's the plan. We'll cover how to protect your cash, the starter methods, Kenton's treasure diving, Moses and stolen cars, gang hideouts, high-end stores, and finally the banks. Stick around for the money cheat at the end, because it's not what most people think.
beats.tts: Here's the plan. We'll cover how to protect your cash, the starter methods, Kenton's treasure diving, Moses and stolen cars, gang hideouts, high-end stores, and finally the banks. Stick around for the money cheat at the end, because it's not what most people think.
beats.visual_need: map of Vice City and Leonida, quick cuts

beats.caption: Let's start with that mistake. At the beginning you don't have a bank account. Every dollar sits in your pocket, and if you die or get busted, that cash is gone.
beats.tts: Let's start with that mistake. At the beginning you don't have a bank account. Every dollar sits in your pocket, and if you die or get busted, that cash is gone.
beats.visual_need: player getting wasted or busted, police arrest

beats.caption: You unlock a bank account in the mission Buck Me, roughly one to two hours into the game. Until then, here's a trick: you can hide cash under the loose floorboards in Jason's bedroom.
beats.tts: You unlock a bank account in the mission Buck Me, roughly one to two hours into the game. Until then, here's a trick: you can hide cash under the loose floorboards in Jason's bedroom.
beats.visual_need: Jason's house interior, bedroom, phone banking app

beats.caption: And even after you have a bank, there's a rule. You can carry a maximum of twenty thousand dollars in cash. Anything above that goes straight into your BuckMe account. So after every big job, find an ATM and deposit.
beats.tts: And even after you have a bank, there's a rule. You can carry a maximum of twenty thousand dollars in cash. Anything above that goes straight into your BuckMe account. So after every big job, find an ATM and deposit.
beats.visual_need: ATM on a Vice City street at night

beats.caption: Now, earning. The first method is available right from the start: store stick-ups. Walk into any grocery store, point your gun at the cashier, and make them open the register. The police response is light, but so is the payout.
beats.tts: Now, earning. The first method is available right from the start: store stick-ups. Walk into any grocery store, point your gun at the cashier, and make them open the register. The police response is light, but so is the payout.
beats.visual_need: convenience store robbery, aiming at cashier, register

beats.caption: The real money isn't in the register. It's in the safe in the back room. The code is often written on a Post-it note somewhere nearby, or you can scare it out of the clerk.
beats.tts: The real money isn't in the register. It's in the safe in the back room. The code is often written on a Post-it note somewhere nearby, or you can scare it out of the clerk.
beats.visual_need: store back room, safe, note on wall

beats.caption: This is where Focus Mode changes everything. Click both sticks at the same time. Cash glows green, useful items glow yellow, and notes with safe codes get highlighted. Doors tell you something too: white means you can go in, red means it's alarmed.
beats.tts: This is where Focus Mode changes everything. Click both sticks at the same time. Cash glows green, useful items glow yellow, and notes with safe codes get highlighted. Doors tell you something too: white means you can go in, red means it's alarmed.
beats.visual_need: slow-motion focus vision, highlighted objects, doors

beats.caption: Mugging is also open from the start, but honestly, it only gets you pocket change. I'd use stick-ups and muggings only when you need a little quick cash. Don't grind them for hours.
beats.tts: Mugging is also open from the start, but honestly, it only gets you pocket change. I'd use stick-ups and muggings only when you need a little quick cash. Don't grind them for hours.
beats.visual_need: mugging a pedestrian on the street

beats.caption: One small purchase pays off on every robbery: a suppressor. Grab one from the Ammu-Nation in Key Lento right after the tutorial. Police respond to gunshot reports, so a suppressor buys you more time to loot.
beats.tts: One small purchase pays off on every robbery: a suppressor. Grab one from the Ammu-Nation in Key Lento right after the tutorial. Police respond to gunshot reports, so a suppressor buys you more time to loot.
beats.visual_need: Ammu-Nation gun store, weapon with suppressor

beats.caption: And the police in GTA 6 don't automatically know everything anymore. They track what you look like. Wear a hat and bandana during the crime, take them off after, keep a spare outfit in your trunk, switch cars, and destroy the CCTV footage in the back room.
beats.tts: And the police in GTA 6 don't automatically know everything anymore. They track what you look like. Wear a hat and bandana during the crime, take them off after, keep a spare outfit in your trunk, switch cars, and destroy the CCTV footage in the back room.
beats.visual_need: police search, character changing clothes, CCTV room

beats.caption: Now the best early-game money. Kenton runs a scuba boat shop in Key Lento, with an illegal side business: underwater treasure diving. Jason does the diving, and in total it can earn you tens of thousands of dollars.
beats.tts: Now the best early-game money. Kenton runs a scuba boat shop in Key Lento, with an illegal side business: underwater treasure diving. Jason does the diving, and in total it can earn you tens of thousands of dollars.
beats.visual_need: boat on clear water, underwater diving

beats.caption: It's not instant money, it takes time. But whenever you're in Key Lento, squeeze in a dive. It runs alongside the story, and before you know it your account is full.
beats.tts: It's not instant money, it takes time. But whenever you're in Key Lento, squeeze in a dive. It runs alongside the story, and before you know it your account is full.
beats.visual_need: Key Lento islands, boat cruising

beats.caption: A simple habit that pays off: every time the story sends you down to Key Lento, plan a dive before you head back. You're already there, so it's free money for a few extra minutes of play.
beats.tts: A simple habit that pays off: every time the story sends you down to Key Lento, plan a dive before you head back. You're already there, so it's free money for a few extra minutes of play.
beats.visual_need: underwater diving, boat returning to shore

beats.caption: Your second big source is cars. In Chapter 2 you meet Moses in Port Gellhorn. He buys stolen cars, but only ones without a tracker.
beats.tts: Your second big source is cars. In Chapter 2 you meet Moses in Port Gellhorn. He buys stolen cars, but only ones without a tracker.
beats.visual_need: stealing a car, driving to a garage

beats.caption: How much does he pay? The guides disagree here. One says one to five thousand dollars per car, another says over ten thousand for a good one. Either way, the better the car, the bigger the payout.
beats.tts: How much does he pay? The guides disagree here. One says one to five thousand dollars per car, another says over ten thousand for a good one. Either way, the better the car, the bigger the payout.
beats.visual_need: luxury cars driving through Vice City

beats.caption: After a sale, Moses goes on cooldown. The fix is simple: sleep at a safehouse and the cooldown resets. Pay N Spray also buys cars, but it has a daily limit and won't take high-end cars with trackers.
beats.tts: After a sale, Moses goes on cooldown. The fix is simple: sleep at a safehouse and the cooldown resets. Pay N Spray also buys cars, but it has a daily limit and won't take high-end cars with trackers.
beats.visual_need: character sleeping in bed, Pay N Spray garage

beats.caption: Before you take a car, open the Waink app on your phone. It shows what security the car has, what it'll sell for, and what it costs to register. Steal blind and you might waste your time.
beats.tts: Before you take a car, open the Waink app on your phone. It shows what security the car has, what it'll sell for, and what it costs to register. Steal blind and you might waste your time.
beats.visual_need: in-game phone app, parked sports car

beats.caption: Later on, in western Vice City, you meet Randy. He hands out contracts for high-end cars, which pay more, and he gives you a key cloner so you can steal keyless electronic cars too.
beats.tts: Later on, in western Vice City, you meet Randy. He hands out contracts for high-end cars, which pay more, and he gives you a key cloner so you can steal keyless electronic cars too.
beats.visual_need: supercar, unlocking a car

beats.caption: Source number three is riskier, but it pays well: rival gang hideouts. When you pass near one, a yellow icon appears on the map, and the map even tells you what's stashed inside.
beats.tts: Source number three is riskier, but it pays well: rival gang hideouts. When you pass near one, a yellow icon appears on the map, and the map even tells you what's stashed inside.
beats.visual_need: shootout at a gang house, map with icons

beats.caption: The drugs you find there vary a lot in value. Weed is cheap, crystal and cocaine are worth far more. You have to carry them to a dealer yourself, someone like Tyrone, who pays you on the spot. You can drop them at a garage later instead, but then the dealer takes a bigger cut.
beats.tts: The drugs you find there vary a lot in value. Weed is cheap, crystal and cocaine are worth far more. You have to carry them to a dealer yourself, someone like Tyrone, who pays you on the spot. You can drop them at a garage later instead, but then the dealer takes a bigger cut.
beats.visual_need: carrying bags to a car, meeting a dealer

beats.caption: Now the big scores. Before banks come high-end stores: the jewelry and clothing shops in Capri, Ocean Beach and Downtown Vice City. Security is tighter, so scout them on the map first to see how much loot there is and how heavily they're guarded.
beats.tts: Now the big scores. Before banks come high-end stores: the jewelry and clothing shops in Capri, Ocean Beach and Downtown Vice City. Security is tighter, so scout them on the map first to see how much loot there is and how heavily they're guarded.
beats.visual_need: luxury jewellery store, Ocean Beach at night

beats.caption: Medium and high security jobs are much easier as a duo. Invite your partner from the map icon. Go in through the back door with a snap gun and the alarm stays quiet. Each character carries two stash bags, a van or truck holds up to eight, and a motorbike holds none.
beats.tts: Medium and high security jobs are much easier as a duo. Invite your partner from the map icon. Go in through the back door with a snap gun and the alarm stays quiet. Each character carries two stash bags, a van or truck holds up to eight, and a motorbike holds none.
beats.visual_need: two characters entering through a back door, loading a van

beats.caption: To sell the jewelry, head to Yasmani in Little Cuba. He pays well for jewelry and marked bills. And remember, loot isn't money until you've sold it.
beats.tts: To sell the jewelry, head to Yasmani in Little Cuba. He pays well for jewelry and marked bills. And remember, loot isn't money until you've sold it.
beats.visual_need: colourful Little Cuba street, handing over a bag

beats.caption: Then come the banks. They open up roughly halfway through the story. Banks use dye packs that explode, so you'll need a dye pack jammer first, which you get in Chapter 3.
beats.tts: Then come the banks. They open up roughly halfway through the story. Banks use dye packs that explode, so you'll need a dye pack jammer first, which you get in Chapter 3.
beats.visual_need: bank exterior, tense heist entry

beats.caption: A bank has three targets: the tellers' cash drawers, safes full of marked bills, and the vault, where the biggest money is. But the moment you walk out, your wanted level goes straight up. It's the biggest payday in the game, and the biggest risk.
beats.tts: A bank has three targets: the tellers' cash drawers, safes full of marked bills, and the vault, where the biggest money is. But the moment you walk out, your wanted level goes straight up. It's the biggest payday in the game, and the biggest risk.
beats.visual_need: bank vault, police chase after a heist

beats.caption: So before any bank job, plan the exit, not just the entry. Park a fast car you haven't been seen in nearby, know where you'll change your outfit, and deposit the cash the moment you're clear. The vault means nothing if you lose it all in the chase.
beats.tts: So before any bank job, plan the exit, not just the entry. Park a fast car you haven't been seen in nearby, know where you'll change your outfit, and deposit the cash the moment you're clear. The vault means nothing if you lose it all in the chase.
beats.visual_need: getaway car, police chase, changing clothes

beats.caption: So where should the money go? My order is simple. First, savings for story missions, because some won't unlock without the cash. Then weapons. Then cars and upgrades. Clothes come last.
beats.tts: So where should the money go? My order is simple. First, savings for story missions, because some won't unlock without the cash. Then weapons. Then cars and upgrades. Clothes come last.
beats.visual_need: shopping montage: gun store, car garage, clothing store

beats.caption: And here's something a lot of players don't know: you can't buy houses or safehouses in GTA 6. The story gives you places to live. So don't save up for property.
beats.tts: And here's something a lot of players don't know: you can't buy houses or safehouses in GTA 6. The story gives you places to live. So don't save up for property.
beats.visual_need: Vice City houses and motel exteriors

beats.caption: And yes, there is a money cheat. It gives you two hundred and fifty thousand dollars every time, but it only unlocks after you finish the main story.
beats.tts: And yes, there is a money cheat. It gives you two hundred and fifty thousand dollars every time, but it only unlocks after you finish the main story.
beats.visual_need: phone in hand, cash

beats.caption: The catch: with cheats on, you can't save, trophies and achievements are disabled, and the money vanishes when you quit. So there's no shortcut early on. You have to earn it.
beats.tts: The catch: with cheats on, you can't save, trophies and achievements are disabled, and the money vanishes when you quit. So there's no shortcut early on. You have to earn it.
beats.visual_need: pause menu

beats.caption: Before the recap, three mistakes I see new players make. Mistake one: carrying a big pile of cash into a fight. If the job goes wrong, that money is gone. Deposit first, then go looking for trouble.
beats.tts: Before the recap, three mistakes I see new players make. Mistake one: carrying a big pile of cash into a fight. If the job goes wrong, that money is gone. Deposit first, then go looking for trouble.
beats.visual_need: shootout, cash counter dropping

beats.caption: Mistake two: robbing a store with your face showing and then driving off in the same car. The police remember your look and your vehicle. A hat, a bandana and a quick car swap make a huge difference.
beats.tts: Mistake two: robbing a store with your face showing and then driving off in the same car. The police remember your look and your vehicle. A hat, a bandana and a quick car swap make a huge difference.
beats.visual_need: police scanning a car, character changing outfit

beats.caption: Mistake three: grinding small jobs for hours. Muggings and stick-ups are fine for a little quick cash, but the real money is in Kenton's dives, Moses's cars, and later the big stores and banks. Play the story to unlock them.
beats.tts: Mistake three: grinding small jobs for hours. Muggings and stick-ups are fine for a little quick cash, but the real money is in Kenton's dives, Moses's cars, and later the big stores and banks. Play the story to unlock them.
beats.visual_need: montage of diving, stolen supercar, bank vault

beats.caption: Quick recap. Early on, a few stick-ups and Moses's car contracts. Start treasure diving as soon as you meet Kenton. Hit gang hideouts when you see the yellow icon. Before banks, the high-end stores in Capri and Ocean Beach. And in the mid game, banks and Randy's contracts.
beats.tts: Quick recap. Early on, a few stick-ups and Moses's car contracts. Start treasure diving as soon as you meet Kenton. Hit gang hideouts when you see the yellow icon. Before banks, the high-end stores in Capri and Ocean Beach. And in the mid game, banks and Randy's contracts.
beats.visual_need: fast recap montage

beats.caption: And the most important rule of all: after every big job, put your money in an ATM. One bad chase and your pocket is empty.
beats.tts: And the most important rule of all: after every big job, put your money in an ATM. One bad chase and your pocket is empty.
beats.visual_need: ATM deposit, then police chase

beats.caption: If you only remember one thing from this video, make it this: the safest money in GTA 6 is the money in your bank, not in your pocket.
beats.tts: If you only remember one thing from this video, make it this: the safest money in GTA 6 is the money in your bank, not in your pocket.
